records.text: Morhan Coppertongue is a metalsmith in Loch Modan who sells goods and offers repairs.
Nillen Andemar is a macecrafter in Loch Modan, offering goods and repairs to visitors.
Karm Ironquill supplies miners in Loch Modan, selling goods to those who need mining supplies.
Kat Sampson is a leather armor merchant in Loch Modan, selling goods and offering repairs.

Mountaineer Cobbleflint calls for help defending the King's lands from the Stonesplinter Troggs and Scouts, which he describes as a growing threat to Loch Modan and Ironforge. His assignment asks adventurers to kill both groups; he points those suited to further work toward Mountaineer Gravelgaw.

Mountaineer Wallbang says the Trogg problem is worsening and the reserves have gone to the front. He challenges a capable adventurer to prove their reputation by hunting Stonesplinter Shamans and Bonesnappers, invoking service to King Magni and Ironforge.

Mountaineer Gravelgaw is a Loch Modan defender who assigns patrol work against the Stonesplinter Troggs. He sends a recruit into the southern hills to kill Skullthumpers and Seers, keeping pressure on the invaders while the defenders await reinforcements. Afterward, he directs the recruit to Mountaineer Wallbang for reassignment.

Captain Rugelfuss commands a regiment assigned to watch Loch Modan’s Gate, a post his troops cannot leave while the Trogg threat looms and the Ironforge Reserve serves at the Alliance front. He asks recruits to bring back Trogg Stone Teeth as proof of an assault in the hills. For a more targeted blow, he identifies chieftain Grawmug and his guards Gnasher and Brawler as the incursion’s leadership, and calls for their elimination to weaken the threat.

Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII oversees engineering concerns at Stonewrought Dam. When he finds strange-smelling powder, he suspects explosives and sends it to Dun Modr expert Ashlan Stonesmirk for analysis. After spotting Dark Iron Insurgents swimming toward the dam with a keg, he prepares a disarming mixture and urgently asks for it to be placed in the keg. He credits the helper with saving the dam and says it is safe for now.

Jern Hornhelm is the Explorers' League contact in Thelsamar for Prospector Ironband's excavation. He handles progress reports and blastpowder requests, and worries that Ironband's slow progress persists despite the supplies already sent. After learning the excavation faces troggs, he wonders whether the powder is being used for digging or fighting, and where an earlier shipment went. He also coordinates supply deliveries through Huldar and the porters.

Magistrate Bluntnose coordinates Thelsamar's defense while the town awaits soldiers from Ironforge. With the town, Stonewrought Dam, and excavation site exposed to ogre attacks, he hires help against the threat and offers compensation for proof of Chok'sul's death. He appreciates efforts that protect the town and hopes to turn attention to the troggs afterward.
Torren Squarejaw is associated with the Explorers' League and is found in Thelsamar.

Marek Ironheart trades in crocolisk meat and skins for hunters at the Farstrider Lodge, while warning that the beasts are ferocious. He recalls nearly losing a hand to one, surviving by jamming a crocolisk's jaws shut with his knife. Marek values hunting skill and praises those who prove themselves, including by besting Daryl.

Kelt Thomasin was once regarded as one of the realm's finest hunters. Now older, he has spent much of his life pursuing a dwarven legend of a huge monster in Loch Modan; he believes he came close to finding it and still encourages the hunt with a mysterious smile.

Vyrin Swiftwind nurses a personal grudge against Daryl the Youngling, whom he calls arrogant and snooty. He recruits help to kill Ol' Sooty, the bear that scarred Daryl, and frames the hunt as payback. Vyrin later shares responsibility for the trophy's disposal, while making a show of disgust at bringing it into the Lodge.

A Stonesplinter Trogg is one of the troggs threatening the Loch: they tunnel up from the ground and are treated as a danger to the region. This trogg's brief aggro cries are blunt commands to destroy, kill, and crush.

A Stonesplinter Scout is among the troggs threatening the Loch, emerging from tunnels with the wider Stonesplinter force. Its brief combat cries urge destruction, killing, and crushing; in combat, the scout also uses Throw.

A Stonesplinter Skullthumper is part of the trogg force threatening the Loch and the southern hills. Its combat cries demand destruction, killing, and crushing; this larger, more experienced variant also uses Gouge in combat.

A Stonesplinter Bonesnapper is a blunt, aggressive trogg fighter whose battle cries reduce its intent to three commands: “Crush,” “Kill,” and “Destroy.” It uses a Strike in combat and may flee for help when badly wounded.

A Stonesplinter Geomancer is a combatant who calls out on engaging a foe and uses Quick Flame Ward in battle. Its cries—“Destroy,” “Kill,” and “Crush”—are terse and aggressive, much like those of other Stonesplinter fighters.

A Stonesplinter Seer is a combatant who uses Lightning Bolt against its foes. Its battle cries—“Destroy,” “Kill,” and “Crush”—are blunt and aggressive, sharing the terse style heard from other Stonesplinter fighters.

A Stonesplinter Digger is a combatant who shouts on engaging a foe. Its cries—“Destroy,” “Kill,” and “Crush”—are blunt and aggressive, matching the terse battle language used by other Stonesplinter fighters.
A Dark Iron Insurgent openly invokes the Dark Iron Dwarves and warns foes never to cross them. Its threats are direct and faction-proud; in battle it can use Stoneform.
A Tunnel Rat Vermin threatens foes and warns them not to take its candle. It cries “Yip! Me kill!” when attacking.
A Tunnel Rat Scout threatens foes and warns them not to take its candle. It can use Shoot in combat.
A Tunnel Rat Geomancer threatens foes and warns them not to take its candle. It can use Quick Flame Ward in combat.
A Tunnel Rat Digger threatens foes and warns them not to take its candle. It can use Defensive Stance in combat.
A Tunnel Rat Forager threatens foes and warns them not to take its candle. It can use Bottle of Poison in combat.
A Tunnel Rat Surveyor threatens foes and warns them not to take its candle. It cries “Yip! Me kill!” when attacking.
A Mo'grosh ogre in the ogre camp by Thelsamar's lake, speaking in blunt threats: “Me smash! You die!” and “I'll crush you!” It can knock opponents down.
A Mo'grosh enforcer in the ogre camp by Thelsamar's lake, barking “Raaar!!!” alongside threats to smash or crush an opponent. Its combat speech is triggered in a fight.
A Mo'grosh brute found around the ogre camp by Thelsamar's lake. It uses the camp's blunt battle cries—“Raaar!!!”, “Me smash! You die!” and “I'll crush you!”—when fighting.

A Mo'grosh shaman in the ogre camp by Thelsamar's lake, threatening to smash or crush opponents. In combat it casts Lightning Bolt, giving this shaman a spellcasting role alongside the camp's blunt battle cries.
A Mo'grosh mystic in the ogre camp by Thelsamar's lake, using the camp's blunt battle cries: “Raaar!!! Me smash $r!”, “Me smash! You die!” and “I'll crush you!” In combat it casts Lightning Bolt.
A Cliff Lurker is a beast who can cast Poison in combat.

Daryl the Youngling, who styles himself Daryl the Bold, turns hunting into a contest and needles challengers before and after they hunt. He boasts of a famous scar from a bear encounter; a bear's head makes him remember it and visibly shake, then he demands that the grisly trophy be removed.
Stonesplinter Shamans are troggs threatening the lands defended by Mountaineer Wallbang. They enter fights with cries of destruction, killing and crushing.
Tunnel Rat Kobolds fiercely defend their candles, threaten opponents and boast that they will not run away.

Grawmug is the Stonesplinter trogg chieftain leading the incursion into Loch Modan, guarded by Gnasher and Brawler. He claims the lands and the Loch for his tribe and taunts opponents as weak or fit for breakfast. He uses Quick Bloodlust in combat and may flee for assistance when badly wounded.
Gnasher is one of the trogg chieftain Grawmug’s elite guards, serving alongside Brawler. Gnasher uses Consume Flesh in combat and may flee for assistance when badly wounded.
Brawler is one of the trogg chieftain Grawmug’s elite guards, serving alongside Gnasher. Brawler uses Backhand in combat.

Chok'sul is an ogre whom Thelsamar's magistrate accuses of coordinating attacks on the town, Stonewrought Dam, and the excavation. His own taunts promise violence, and one reveals an appetite for eating his foes.
Aldren Cordon is Thelsamar's clothier, offering goods and repairs to visitors. His trade serves a practical part of the town's daily life.

The Dark Iron Sapper threatens Stonewrought Dam, invoking the fall of Thandol Span as a precedent. It fights in Ragnaros's name and denounces King Magni Bronzebeard, making its allegiance and target plain.
Mountaineer Brokk is a named mountaineer of Loch Modan, identified by both his personal name and role title.

Mountaineer Kadrell treats the tunnel-rat kobold infestation west of Thelsamar as a serious local problem and offers a bounty for their ears; he ruefully notes their smell when paying it. He enjoys his brother’s Shimmer Stout, joking that it turns his head and lightens his limbs. He welcomes visitors and points those willing to serve the Alliance toward the Explorers’ League duty notice.

Mountaineer Rockgar seeks volunteers for a mission through Dun Algaz into the Wetlands. What begins as scouting has become a messier operation, and he checks that recruits are ready for the change in danger. His mission reflects concern over the Dragonmaw foothold in Dun Algaz, which threatens the route between Loch Modan and Menethil Harbor.

Mountaineer Stormpike is stationed at Loch Modan’s northern guard tower, where guarding duty limits the tasks he can take on himself. He asks travelers to recover Miners’ League gear from kobold-held Silver Stream Mine before Mountaineers move in, and resents the kobolds’ presence there. He also commissions a shield from the Stormwind armorsmith Furen Longbeard and receives an axe made by Grimand, eager to test it against troggs and kobolds. His delivery quests show a personal interest in finely made arms and armor.

Prospector Ironband leads an excavation near Loch Modan and pursues the question of whether ancient artifacts provoked the troggs. He compares the idols found at his site with urns from Agmond's Badlands dig, seeking evidence for a link. Agmond's death weighs on him; he remembers the fellow prospector as a formidable fighter and wants his report and findings carried forward.

Magmar Fellhew manages the details at Ironband's excavation and investigates the carved idols found there. He says the idols drive troggs berserk, and wants them recovered for study and kept from trogg hands. Reporting the site's slowdown to Jern, he identifies the troggs as the cause. He is alert to the danger at the site and sees promise in capable visitors.
Gothor Brumn is an armorer who offers goods for sale and repair. His services support practical equipment needs.

Miran is a one-handed powder hauler tasked with taking the shipment to Prospector Ironband at the excavation site. After an earlier ambush by Saean and other Dark Irons, he worries about further threats and welcomes an escort. He checks the barrels and speaks defiantly when attacked, though he admits his injured hand leaves him poorly able to defend himself.
A berserk trogg that attacks with blunt cries to destroy, kill, and crush. Its brief speech accompanies aggression rather than conversation.

Boss Galgosh is identified as a Stonesplinter chieftain. He threatens intruders, calls for their deaths, and claims the Loch and surrounding lands for his tribe. In combat he can frenzy; his words express the tribe's territorial hostility.
Magosh is identified as a Stonesplinter tribal shaman. In combat, Magosh uses lightning and shock and voices the tribe's claims to the Loch and its hostility toward outsiders.
Grizlak uses Renew when nearby allies are badly wounded and may flee for assistance when badly wounded.
Drac Roughcut is a tradesman who sells goods.
Vrok Blunderblast is a gunsmith who repairs equipment.

Ghak Healtouch is an alchemy trainer in Thelsamar who takes pride in his restorative brews. He gathers Badlands reagents and seeks magenta fungus caps from Uldaman to study their alchemical potential. He acknowledges the danger of collecting dragon blood but offers a restorative recipe as a reward, stressing risk and reward. He speaks fondly of Kali, calling her the apple of his eye.
Kali Healtouch teaches herbalism.
Rann Flamespinner keeps tailoring supplies in Thelsamar. Travelers can browse his goods, giving him a practical role in the town’s daily trade.

Thorgrum Borrelson is Thelsamar’s gryphon master, offering paid rides on his gryphons. He calls them the fastest in the Eastern Kingdoms and sends travelers onward to Ironforge. He also directs people carrying Brock’s list of mining students to Golnir Bouldertoe, who prepares their honorary picks. His work connects local mining lessons with Ironforge, while his gryphon service helps travelers make the journey.

Brock Stoneseeker trains miners in Thelsamar and looks after young dwarves learning the trade. He recognizes students who excel by awarding honorary picks, then arranges for the picks to be prepared in Ironforge and returned to his students for use in Loch Modan. His pride in mining comes through in his advice: a good miner needs a firm grip, a stout heart, and hair thick with black dust.
Yanni Stoutheart stocks general supplies in Thelsamar, including ammunition. His shop serves the town’s everyday needs and gives travelers a place to browse practical goods.

Warg Deepwater is a fishing trainer. When a learner has outgrown his instruction, he points them toward Old Man Heming’s copy of “The Bass and You” or Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh for further guidance.
Khara Deepwater is a fishing supplies vendor in the Loch Modan area, offering goods to visitors.
Xandar Goodbeard is a general supplies vendor in the Loch Modan area, offering goods to visitors.
Irene Sureshot is a gunsmith in the Loch Modan area. She offers goods and repair services.
Cliff Hadin is a bowyer in the Loch Modan area. He offers ammunition and repair services.
Loch Crocolisks are beasts found around Loch Modan, including its lake and nearby wetlands.
Dakk Blunderblast is a humanoid in Loch Modan.

Vidra handles the cooking behind Thelsamar's blood sausages. She asks for bear meat, boar intestines, and spider ichor, then prepares the meal herself and shares the recipe. Her cooking serves the town's hungry children and excavation workers.

Huldar oversees blast-powder deliveries to the excavation, splitting the work with Miran while he watches the remaining barrels. After a Dark Iron ambush, he worries Miran cannot safely carry the next shipment alone. Learning Saean may have sympathized with the attackers shakes him; they had worked together for nearly a year. Even so, Huldar insists the deliveries must continue.

Deek Fizzlebizz is an engineering trainer who wonders where he left his spinner.
Greishan Ironstove is a traveling merchant who offers goods and calls out fresh bread for sale.
Claude Erksine is a pet trainer who says he only helps hunters and their pets.

Mountaineer Pebblebitty guards the Searing Gorge gate and is fiercely protective of her authority over access. Margol’s gigantic horn carries the broken axe head bearing Pebblebitty’s name, tying her to a past encounter with the beast. She initially rejects a presented horn as a fake, insisting Margol’s is far larger; Curator Thorius later says she wanted to kill Margol herself because of “the incident.” Once the player returns with Thorius’s proof of deed, she honors the deal and gives the key, though she doubts the player’s strength and warns them of the danger ahead.
Honni Goldenoat is a baker in Dun Morogh who also offers goods for sale.

Thorvald Deepforge helps keep Loch Modan’s mountaineers supplied with weapons and armor in their fight against the troggs. His colleague asks for copper axes and chain belts to be brought to him. Thorvald has little time to chat and offers armor plans in thanks for supplies.

Bailor Stonehand has agreed to provide Jordan with alloy for Ironforge. He reports that Mo’grosh ogres ambushed the ore caravan from the Wetlands and that its surviving guard died before a healer could reach him. Bailor directs a search across the Loch and promises to honor his deal when the ore is recovered.

Bingles Blastenheimer was sent to reconnoiter Gnomeregan but crashed his gyrocopter in Loch Modan. He says troggs stole his tools and Blastencapper explosives, and asks for their return to help the movement prepare a gnomish air assault. He questions Gnoarn’s trust in his reconnaissance before urgently seeking help.
Innkeeper Hearthstove tends an inn in Loch Modan, inviting guests to fill a tankard and share stories. Visitors can find lodging, goods, and a seasonal Trick or Treat exchange.
Thragomm is a Horde runner and quest contact.
A mountaineer serving in Thelsamar.
Lina Hearthstove is a stable master in Loch Modan who offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Dargh Trueaim is a hunter trainer in Loch Modan who speaks in a rough dialect. He offers hunter training, while his greeting directs characters he cannot train to a trainer for their class.
Shanda the Spinner is a rare beast.
Emogg the Crusher is a named combatant who threatens to smash or crush opponents, including a blunt warning that they will die. His short combat barks portray him as eager to fight.
Lord Condar is a formidable named beast found in several areas. In combat, he casts a spell.
Elder Silvervein is a festival elder whose greeting describes the ancients awakening as the year turns and the moon shines bright. Her gossip points visitors toward Elder Goldwell and Elder Ironband.

The Loch Modan Flame Warden is an Alliance-aligned festival attendant who invites visitors to honor the local flame. The warden urges respect for fires in Alliance settlements and describes Horde fires as unworthy, encouraging their desecration. The associated festival quest calls for honoring the Loch Modan flame.

place_records.text: You are in Loch Modan, Alliance land in the Eastern Kingdoms. Thelsamar, Stonewrought Dam and the Farstrider Lodge are its main settlements, all kept by the Alliance. Stonesplinter troggs, Mo'grosh ogres and tunnel rat kobolds trouble the land, and Dark Iron insurgents have been seen swimming toward the Dam.

You are in Ironband's Excavation Site, a dig in Loch Modan that Prospector Ironband leads. Magmar Fellhew manages its details and says the carved idols found here drive troggs berserk. Stonesplinter diggers and geomancers haunt the ruins.

You are in Mo'grosh Stronghold, a fortress in Loch Modan held by Mo'grosh ogres, with enforcers, brutes, shamans and mystics among them. Bailor Stonehand reports that Mo'grosh ogres ambushed an ore caravan from the Wetlands.

You are in Thelsamar, the Alliance town of Loch Modan, with its inn and a gryphon master, Thorgrum Borrelson, who sends travelers onward to Ironforge. Brock Stoneseeker trains miners here, and Jern Hornhelm handles the excavation's reports. Magistrate Bluntnose coordinates the town's defense, since ogre attacks threaten it while it awaits soldiers from Ironforge.

You are in Stonewrought Dam, an Alliance works in Loch Modan overseen by Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Dark Iron insurgents were seen swimming toward the Dam with a large keg. Loch frenzies and tunnel rat kobolds also trouble the area.

You are in The Farstrider Lodge, an Alliance hunting lodge in Loch Modan. Dargh Trueaim trains hunters, and Marek Ironheart trades crocolisk meat and skins for them. Daryl the Youngling turns hunting into a contest, and mountain buzzards and grizzled black bears are hunted here.

You are in Silver Stream Mine, an old Loch Modan mine that ran dry long ago. The Miners' League turned it into a storage depot, but kobolds have moved in, along with tunnel rat diggers and geomancers.

You are in The Loch, the lake of Loch Modan. Warg Deepwater trains fishers, and Khara Deepwater sells fishing supplies. Loch crocolisks and loch frenzies make the water dangerous, and Dark Iron ambushes have hit powder shipments bound for the excavation.
You are in Dun Algaz, a post on the road from Loch Modan to the Wetlands, where Dragonmaw orcs have pushed in from their haven in the Wetlands. Mountaineer Rockgar runs scouting missions through it.

You are in Stonesplinter Valley, where Stonesplinter troggs, seers, skullthumpers and scouts are common. Shadowforge diggers work among them, and the dwarf Hammertoe Grez, wounded, is held in Uldaman.

You are in Valley of Kings, where Alliance mountaineers hold the southern guard tower. Captain Rugelfuss commands a regiment watching Loch Modan's Gate, and Mountaineer Pebblebitty guards the Searing Gorge gate, fiercely protective of her authority over access. Stonesplinter troggs and scouts press on the defenders.

You are in Algaz Station, the Alliance post at Loch Modan's northern guard tower. Mountaineer Stormpike keeps watch there, and the Miners' League's gear still lies in the kobold-held Silver Stream Mine.
You are in Grizzlepaw Ridge, a rise in Loch Modan. Grizzled black bears and Black Bear Patriarchs roam it, and a bear called Ol' Sooty is known here.
